on Monday questioned

Jensen Huang
as CEO, days after telling
Bitcoin
investors to sell.
Schiff Asks If Nvidia Just Reset Corporate Conduct Standards
Huang resigned earlier this month amid reports of extramarital relationships, and Schiff questioned what his return signals for workplace rules.
"Does Jensen Huang being reinstated as $NVDA’s CEO mean that now it’s OK for CEOs to have affairs with their subordinates?
How far down the corporate ladder does this new standard apply? What about sexual harassment? Are we now back to the Mad Men days?" he noted.
Nvidia’s board reversed course fast after Chair
Harvey Jones
told investors on Nov. 17 that it "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," citing conduct that conflicted with company standards, and said Nvidia had already hired a firm to find his successor.
Six days later, that same board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, saying it had consulted senior U.S. officials and concluded his return posed no national security risk.
Independent directors are still investigating separate reports that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him.

Elon Musk welcomed Huang’s return, writing that "the mistake has been corrected," while investor Michael Burry called Nvidia "weaker, more craven than even I thought" and urged regulators to keep investigating.
Schiff Also Questions Who Bought Nvidia Before the Rally
In a separate post, Schiff speculated that people close to President
Donald Trump
bought Nvidia and other AI stocks near Friday’s close, betting that Trump’s push for Huang’s reinstatement would hit social media before Monday’s open.
He named no buyers and offered no evidence.

Trump had publicly backed Huang’s return Friday, repeated the appeal on Truth Social Sunday night, and told CNBC Monday he’d personally urged the board to act, saying "we have to protect our geniuses, and he is certainly a genius."
Schiff’s Bitcoin Warnings Haven’t Let Up
Schiff’s Nvidia questions come
pressing the opposite case on crypto. On Nov. 19, with Bitcoin down nearly $25,000 in seven weeks, he argued "gold shouldn’t have gone down at all and Bitcoin hasn’t gone down enough."
